human_check: Two things are true here and the port acted on both. The strip fix worked: the warp graphics pipeline creates, so R6's driver half is confirmed from this side even though the driver's own case is still red on its harness. And the next stop is the compute variant of the same effect, which the port does not need: r_waterwarpcompute defaults to 1 but the raster path does the same job through the strip pipeline the driver just learned, so the port defaults it to 0 as a registered accommodation with a retirement trigger (the driver's compute path taking the bindings its graphics path already takes). That is not a workaround for R6 - the raster path is upstream's own code. The driver item that remains is R7: the lightmap update compute pass genuinely needs several bindings (a storage image and two sampled images), so the compute path has to grow regardless, just not before the first frame.
